raw_response:
Alright, let me sit down and think through the year. I'm 68 now, been working this 7.5 mu for 20 years. My wife still helps me in the field, my son works in the city and sends money home, and the grandkids come back for the busy season sometimes. I can't swing a hoe like I used to, so I plan things so I don't have to rush.

**The main fields — wheat and maize (6 mu)**

The wheat went in last October. It's up now and starting to joint — I already gave it the green-up water in March. Planted a local strong-stalk variety, seed I mostly saved from last year plus a bit bought from the township co-op. Before planting I put down about two bags of compound fertilizer per mu (that's 15-15-15, so roughly 7-8 kg N per mu as base), and I'll topdress 10 kg of urea per mu at jointing in the next week or two — that gives me another 4-5 kg N. Total about 12-13 kg N per mu. The extension fellow said 15 is the target but at my age I don't push it — too much and the wheat lodges, and urea prices this year are still high.

I'll water it two more times — one at jointing, one at grain filling. Well water isn't cheap, about 30 yuan per mu per watering with the electric pump. If it rains enough in May I'll skip the grain-filling water. I sprayed once for aphids last week, cheap stuff from the agricultural supply shop. Should get around 450 kg per mu if the weather holds — last year I got 470, year before 420 from the late frost.

Right after wheat harvest in mid-June I'll plant maize on the same fields — no time to plow properly, I'll do no-till direct seeding like everyone around here. Hire the neighbor with the planter, 15 yuan per mu. Buy hybrid seed (Zhengdan 958 or whatever they have), can't save hybrid seed. Base compound fertilizer at planting, topdress urea at big trumpet stage — similar N rate, maybe 13-14 kg/mu. One irrigation in July usually, more if July is dry. Spray once for armyworm if I see them. Harvest around October 1st, about 500 kg per mu if it's a normal year.

**The vegetable plots (1.5 mu)**

These are my wife's babies — half a mu each of cabbage, chili, and eggplant. We sell to the traders who come to the village and eat what doesn't sell. Vegetables need more fertilizer and more spraying than grain, but the money per mu is much better.

Cabbage I transplant in early April (already in the ground), harvest late May. Put down manure from the old neighbor's pig shed plus compound fertilizer. Spray for cabbage worm maybe 3 times through the season.

Chili and eggplant go in mid-late April, start picking in June and keep picking till September. These need staking, drip tubes (I have a simple setup from a few years back), and more pesticide because aphids and the stem borer are bad. My wife does most of the picking — I just help with the heavy stuff.

**The honest tradeoffs**

At my age I don't take risks. I use what I know works. I could push fertilizer higher and maybe get more yield, but extra 200 yuan on inputs for a maybe 30 kg yield bump isn't worth it to me when I don't know if the price will be good. I keep a little cash reserve — last year my wife had a hospital bill, and I was glad I hadn't spent everything on fertilizer.
